item.title: Escambia County Clerk's Office Hiring Part-Time Student Assistant
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Clerk and Comptroller's Office is looking to fill a part-time student assistant position at the Billy G. Ward Century Courthouse in north Escambia County. The position, based at 7500 North Century Boulevard, pays $15 per hour and is available for up to 1,400 hours per fiscal year. Interested applicants will handle filing,…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Clerk and Comptroller's Office is looking to fill a part-time student assistant position at the Billy G. Ward Century Courthouse in north Escambia County.

The position, based at 7500 North Century Boulevard, pays $15 per hour and is available for up to 1,400 hours per fiscal year. Interested applicants will handle filing, pulling court dockets, preparing documents, operating scanners, and delivering records as part of their duties.

The office is now accepting applications for the role. Those interested can contact the Clerk and Comptroller's Office for more information on how to apply.

item.title: Pine Meadow third graders explore UF/IFAS Extension in world tour activity
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: UF/IFAS Extension in Escambia County recently welcomed 130 third grade students from Pine Meadow Elementary School for an interactive learning event that introduced them to the organization's work in the community. Students participated in a "world travel" themed program where they moved through different stations, each designed to highlight…
item.content:encoded:
UF/IFAS Extension in Escambia County recently welcomed 130 third grade students from Pine Meadow Elementary School for an interactive learning event that introduced them to the organization's work in the community.

Students participated in a "world travel" themed program where they moved through different stations, each designed to highlight various aspects of Extension's mission. Every child received a passport that was stamped at each location, turning the educational experience into an engaging adventure.

The event showcased how Extension impacts local life, from agriculture and natural resources to family and consumer sciences. By introducing young students to Extension's programs early, organizers aim to build awareness about the organization's role in supporting Escambia County residents.

item.title: Ex-Pensacola Police Officer Facing Felony Charges Over Illegal Sexual Material
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A former Pensacola Police officer has been arrested and faces dozens of felony charges related to the possession of illegal sexual material, according to an arrest report released this week. Matthew Hale Baxter, 47, is accused of storing prohibited content across multiple personal electronic devices. According to the report, investigators…
item.content:encoded:
A former Pensacola Police officer has been arrested and faces dozens of felony charges related to the possession of illegal sexual material, according to an arrest report released this week.

Matthew Hale Baxter, 47, is accused of storing prohibited content across multiple personal electronic devices. According to the report, investigators discovered more than 1,800 files related to bestiality, as well as child abuse material, during their investigation.

The charges represent one of the most serious criminal allegations involving a Pensacola Police Department employee in recent years. The department has not yet issued a public statement regarding the case or any internal disciplinary actions taken in connection with Baxter's employment.

item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment man is facing felony charges after Escambia County Sheriff's Office deputies discovered him with a stolen motorcycle at a convenience store on Muscogee Road, according to an arrest report.

Deputies apprehended Austin Devon Gillenwater in connection with the stolen vehicle. The arrest report indicates the motorcycle was reported stolen, and Gillenwater was found in possession of it at the time of the stop.

The arrest is the latest in a series of property crime cases handled by ECSO in the North Escambia area. Gillenwater remains in custody pending further court proceedings.

item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment resident is back in custody after authorities say he removed his court-ordered electronic monitoring device less than a week after being released from prison. Robert Lewis Bassett, Jr., 49, was booked into the Escambia County Jail on charges of tampering with an electronic monitoring device and grand theft, according to local reporting.

Details about where the ankle monitor was found or the circumstances leading to Bassett's arrest were not immediately available. The quick return to jail underscores challenges some former inmates face in complying with supervision conditions following their release from the Florida Department of Corrections.

Bassett remains in the Escambia County Jail pending further court proceedings. The case is being handled through the local criminal justice system.

item.title: Ascension Sacred Heart launches ECMO transport training for critical patients
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Ascension Sacred Heart Hospital in Pensacola is rolling out specialized training for a potentially life-saving technology that could transform how the hospital handles its most critically ill patients. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation — ECMO — is an artificial life support system that takes over the work of the heart and lungs, delivering…
item.content:encoded:
Ascension Sacred Heart Hospital in Pensacola is rolling out specialized training for a potentially life-saving technology that could transform how the hospital handles its most critically ill patients. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation — ECMO — is an artificial life support system that takes over the work of the heart and lungs, delivering oxygen directly to the body when those organs fail.

The new training program will prepare staff to safely transport patients who depend on ECMO support, expanding the hospital's capacity to move patients between facilities or to specialized care units. ECMO is typically reserved for patients with severe heart or lung failure who haven't responded to conventional treatments, and the ability to transport these patients safely opens new possibilities for connecting them with advanced care options.

The upgrade reflects Ascension Sacred Heart's commitment to expanding critical care capabilities in Pensacola and the surrounding region. As one of the area's major medical centers, the hospital has been investing in advanced technologies and training to handle complex medical emergencies.

The state senator has also raised questions about the Elmore County prison construction process that he believes warrant formal review.

The Escambia County prison project has been a topic of discussion at the county level as officials work to address capacity and facility needs. Ledbetter's call for investigation and work stoppage could affect the timeline for the local facility's completion.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County has received a FEMA Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, opening the door for residents to apply for federal aid.

The declaration allows eligible county residents to seek FEMA support for disaster-related damages and losses. Residents can apply for assistance through FEMA's registration process, which typically includes documenting damage, providing proof of residency, and meeting other eligibility requirements.

For more information on how to apply or to check eligibility, residents should visit FEMA's official website or contact their local emergency management office.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Opens Debris Removal Info Line for Storm Cleanup
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The line, available at 833-495-3919, operates seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., according to the county's Communications & Media Relations office. Residents can call to ask about…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is reminding residents that a dedicated Debris Removal Information Line is now open to help with questions about ongoing storm cleanup efforts. The line, available at 833-495-3919, operates seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., according to the county's Communications & Media Relations office.

Residents can call to ask about proper debris placement, pickup schedules, the debris removal process, or to report concerns. The county emphasizes that residents should not contact 911 or Santa Rosa County Emergency Management for debris-related questions — the dedicated info line is the appropriate resource.

The debris collection effort is expected to take several weeks to complete. The county says that proper placement of storm debris helps crews work safely and efficiently, and residents are urged to follow county debris removal guidelines. More information is available at www.santarosa.fl.gov/DebrisInfo.

item.title: Pensacola Hurricane Isaias Public Damage and Recovery Costs Top $47 Million
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The City of Pensacola now estimates Hurricane Isaias caused more than $47 million in damage to public facilities and government recovery costs, while crews continue a debris operation expected to last several more weeks. The latest assessment includes approximately $16 million in projected debris-removal costs.…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The City of Pensacola now estimates Hurricane Isaias caused more than $47 million in damage to public facilities and government recovery costs, while crews continue a debris operation expected to last several more weeks.

The latest assessment includes approximately $16 million in projected debris-removal costs.

Another $24.5 million involves damage to city-owned buildings, parks and other facilities, including Pensacola International Airport, the Port of Pensacola, fire stations and community facilities.

The figure is separate from the city's earlier estimate of more than $71 million in damage to privately owned property.

The new federal Major Disaster Declaration means eligible city expenses can now qualify for FEMA Public Assistance.

Reeves said the federal reimbursement could cover roughly $12 million of the city's projected $16 million debris bill.

Pensacola has collected approximately 347,000 cubic yards of hurricane debris so far.

About two-thirds of city roads have received at least some debris collection, although city officials emphasize that does not mean those streets are finished.

The contractor estimates it will take approximately three more weeks to complete the first full collection pass.

A second pass will begin immediately afterward.

The city has also established a dedicated debris hotline at 833-495-3573 for residents with questions about pickup, eligible debris and how material should be prepared.

The hotline operates from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m., seven days a week.

FEMA Individual Assistance for residents remains under federal review.
